cards.title: Three workspace screens: Agents, Board and Terminals
cards.user_does: Clicks Agents, Board or Terminals in the switch at the top of the window.
cards.user_sees: The workspace swaps between an agent-centred list with chat, a status board of every session, and the classic terminal grid; the same sessions keep running underneath.
rules: The switch sits in the full-width top bar of the new look; the classic look has no switch and stays on the terminal grid.
When no view was ever chosen the workspace opens on Board.
Switching screens never closes, restarts or remounts a running terminal.
acceptance: New look on, click each of the three labels → each screen renders and the selected label is highlighted.
Start an agent on Terminals, switch to Board and back → same pane, same scrollback, process still running.

cards.title: Cycle the workspace screen from the keyboard
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+Alt+V, or picks a screen from View > Workspace View.
cards.user_sees: The workspace moves to the next screen in the order Agents, Board, Terminals; the menu lists the three screens as radio items with the current one checked.
rules: The order matches the order of the labels in the top-bar switch.
The chord does nothing in the classic look, where there is no top bar.
The chord is rebindable like every other shortcut.
The submenu appears only when the top bar is on.
The menu rebuilds whenever the screen or the top-bar setting changes, so the check mark never lags.
The cycle line is a hint; the renderer owns the chord.
acceptance: New look, on Agents, press the chord three times → Board, Terminals, Agents.
Classic look, press the chord → nothing changes.
Switch to Board with the mouse, open the menu → Board is checked.
Turn the new look off → the submenu is gone.

cards.title: Full-width top bar with search hint and inbox bell
cards.user_does: Looks at the top of the window in the new look; clicks the search hint or the bell.
cards.user_sees: A bar spanning the whole window above the sidebar row, carrying the window's left controls, the screen switch, a search hint, a bell and the usage pill. The search hint opens the worktree palette; the bell opens the Inbox.
rules: Classic chrome keeps a sidebar-width title header and no top bar.
The top bar never overlaps the native window controls on Windows.
acceptance: Click the search hint → the worktree palette opens with focus in its input.
Click the bell → the Inbox page opens.

cards.title: No worktree sidebar on Agents and Board
cards.user_does: Switches between the three screens in the new look.
cards.user_sees: Agents and Board take the full width with no classic worktree sidebar; Terminals keeps the sidebar.
rules: The hide rule applies only in the new look; the classic look keeps the sidebar everywhere.
Hiding the sidebar never unmounts the terminal workbench behind it.
acceptance: New look: Agents and Board show no worktree list; Terminals shows it.
Classic look: the sidebar is visible on every screen.

cards.title: The app reopens on the screen and page you left
cards.user_does: Leaves Kolux on a screen or a full page (for example Tasks), quits and restarts.
cards.user_sees: Kolux comes back on that same screen or page.
rules: Rapid switches collapse into one saved write; the last choice is flushed synchronously when the window closes.
An unknown or missing saved page falls back to the terminal workspace.
A page whose titlebar button is hidden still restores if it was the last one open.
A corrupt preference file is ignored, not fatal; older saved values migrate.
Nothing is written until startup has finished loading the saved state, and a later cross-window sync never overwrites the current page.
acceptance: Open Tasks, quit, relaunch → Tasks is shown.
Corrupt the saved preference file, relaunch → app opens on the terminal workspace without an error dialog.

cards.title: Each workspace screen can have its own theme
cards.user_does: Picks a theme override for one of the three screens.
cards.user_sees: That screen paints in its own theme; screens without an override follow the global theme.
rules: A screen with no saved value counts as Terminals for theme purposes.
The classic look ignores Board and Agents overrides.
acceptance: Give Board a dark override, keep global light → Board is dark, Terminals is light.
Turn the new look off → the Board override no longer applies.

cards.title: Screen and sidebar preferences stay in step across windows
cards.user_does: Changes the workspace screen or the sleeping-workspaces toggle in one Kolux window.
cards.user_sees: Other open windows pick up the same preference; the toggle survives a restart.
rules: A sync from another window never yanks the current window off a page the user is on.
acceptance: Two windows open, hide sleeping workspaces in one → the other hides them too.

cards.title: Weekly usage pill in the top right
cards.user_does: Glances at the top-right corner.
cards.user_sees: One small pill per provider showing how much of the weekly allowance is left, tinted by how full it is.
rules: Only the weekly window counts; the 5-hour window is ignored.
Providers that report only a 5-hour window get no pill.
With no usage data the pill is not drawn at all.
This replaced the status-bar usage chips on 2026-10-05.
Pills exist only for Claude and Codex; no other provider ever gets one.
A provider shows only while its usage item is ticked in the status-bar item list and its agent CLI is installed.
Hovering a pill shows a countdown to the weekly reset, or says the reset time is unknown.
acceptance: Signed-in Claude with weekly data → a pill with a remaining percentage.
No provider data → no pill and no empty placeholder.

cards.title: Full-page views open over the workspace
cards.user_does: Opens Tasks, Automations, Skills, Artifacts, Space, Inbox, Floor or Settings; presses Mod+Shift+3 to leave.
cards.user_sees: The page fills the workspace area; Show Code closes it and returns to the terminal workspace; the top-bar bell opens Inbox.
rules: Only one full page is open at a time.
Right-sidebar controls are suppressed while a full page is showing.
The page list is fixed; unknown page ids are rejected.
Sibling page shortcuts for Floor and Inbox exist but ship unbound.
Its own shortcut exists but is unbound by default.
The list's contents and rules belong to the agent-status area.
Escape first closes any open menu, popover or dialog; only when none is showing does it leave the full page. Hidden overlays do not count.
acceptance: Open Tasks then press Show Code → back on the workspace screen.
Open Settings → the right sidebar controls are hidden.
On Skills, press the chord → workspace screen shown.
Click the bell → Inbox page shown.
cards.compat: keybinding ids view.code (default Mod+Shift+3), view.inbox and view.floor (unbound)

cards.title: Tasks page button and shortcut
cards.user_does: Clicks the Tasks button in the title bar, or a bound shortcut.
cards.user_sees: The Tasks page for GitHub issues and pull requests.
rules: The title-bar button is on by default and can be hidden from View > Appearance.
The default task source is GitHub and the default preset shows everything.
The shortcut ships unbound.
Other task providers are cut; the page becomes GitHub-only.
acceptance: Fresh profile → a Tasks button is visible; clicking it opens the GitHub task list.

cards.title: Automations and Skills pages
cards.user_does: Turns on the Automations or Skills title-bar button, or opens either page.
cards.user_sees: The Automations or Skills page; whichever was open at quit is restored after a restart.
rules: The button is off by default.
The page stays; its settings section is cut.
acceptance: Enable the button → it appears in the title bar and opens the page.
Open Skills, restart → Skills is shown.

cards.title: Artifacts library
cards.user_does: Opens the Artifacts page, adds a file with Add artifact, types in the search box, selects an item, or removes one.
cards.user_sees: A list of saved artifacts, newest first, each with its title, size and source; selecting one shows a preview beside the list; a remove button takes it out of the library.
rules: Search matches titles only and requires every typed word to appear.
An empty library and a search with no matches show different messages.
Sizes read in B, KB or MB with one decimal.
Each preview gets a stable page identity so reopening the same artifact reuses it.
acceptance: Add two files → newest is on top.
Search two words where only one matches a title → that item is hidden.
Remove the selected item → it leaves the list and the preview closes.

cards.title: Floor timeline of agent activity
cards.user_does: Opens the Floor page and picks a range of 15 minutes, 60 minutes or today.
cards.user_sees: One lane per agent session with coloured segments for working, needs-you and idle over time, and six time ticks along the axis.
rules: Blocked and waiting both show as needs-you.
Segments are clamped to the chosen range; today starts at local midnight.
A lane with no live terminal evidence shows as unverifiable rather than idle.
Child sessions nest under their parent; the local machine's lanes come first.
Floor left the sidebar on 2026-09-22; it is reachable by an unbound shortcut.
acceptance: Range today at 09:00 → axis starts at local midnight.
An agent blocked on approval for 5 minutes → a needs-you segment of that length.

cards.title: Space view: disk use per worktree and bulk delete
cards.user_does: Opens the Space page, sorts or searches the table, ticks rows and deletes.
cards.user_sees: A treemap of the biggest items plus a sortable, searchable table of worktrees with size, file count and age; only the deletable selected worktrees are removed.
rules: The treemap keeps a fixed square layout and folds the tail into one omitted-items block.
Sizes, counts and relative ages are formatted for reading, not raw numbers.
Rows mark worktrees in active use: open browsers or running agents.
Git status refreshes the active worktree first, then the visible ones, then the rest.
A deletable-only filter narrows the table.
Worktrees in active use are never deletable from here.
acceptance: Sort the table by size → biggest first.
Search a branch name → only matching rows remain.
Select one deletable and one active worktree, delete → only the deletable one goes.

cards.title: Agents screen lists sessions by saved agent
cards.user_does: Opens the Agents screen.
cards.user_sees: A rail of sessions grouped under each saved agent, with AI sessions that match no saved agent under an Other sessions group; selecting one shows it on the right.
rules: Plain shell terminals are never listed.
On first open the first agent with sessions is chosen, on its newest session; afterwards the last selection is remembered.
In the new look the rail is a 268px rounded card; otherwise a flat 240px rail.

A row started by the orchestrator is named by its task's display name or title, then by the task text pulled from the dispatch prompt, and only otherwise by the raw prompt; dispatch boilerplate is never shown.
acceptance: One saved agent with two sessions plus one unmatched Codex session → two groups; the unmatched one sits under Other sessions.
Select a session, switch screens and back → same session selected.

cards.title: One line per session says what the agent is doing
cards.user_does: Scans the Agents rail.
cards.user_sees: Under each session a short line: what an approval is asking for, the current step while working, idle with how long, or a fresh Done with how recently.
rules: When several signals compete the most urgent wins: approval, then working, then done, then idle.
With no evidence the line stays empty rather than guessing.
acceptance: Agent waiting on a file-edit approval → line names that approval.
Agent idle 12 minutes → line says idle with the duration.

cards.title: Fixed status words on the Agents screen
cards.user_does: Reads a session's status label.
cards.user_sees: One of a frozen set of words: working, needs you, done, stopped, idle, starting, not started, or that the host can't be reached.
rules: A stale working reading is never shown as working.
An unreachable host shows a can't-reach word instead of the last known state.
A pane with no process yet shows starting; a preset that was never launched shows not started.
acceptance: Kill the agent's process without a done signal → label leaves working within the staleness window.

cards.title: Usage line on the Agents screen
cards.user_does: Looks at the selected session's usage line.
cards.user_sees: A rounded percentage of the plan's 5-hour window and the local time it resets.
rules: Follows the user's used-or-remaining display preference.
Never prints a not-a-number value.
Says nothing when the provider has no 5-hour window.
acceptance: Claude at 37.6 % used, preference used → shows 38 % and a local reset time.

cards.title: Chat, terminal and composer for the selected session
cards.user_does: Selects a session on the Agents screen, types in its composer, or flips the Show terminal switch.
cards.user_sees: Supported agents show as a chat thread with a composer that sends to that agent; plain terminals and unsupported agents show their terminal; the switch forces the terminal.
rules: Chat shows for supported agents even when the global chat experiment is off.
A session that has not started yet shows an agent chooser instead.
Claude chat runs through a bridge with the terminal one switch away.
This composer is the one typing surface outside the terminal; the terminal-grid message bar was removed on 2026-10-05.
A live agent detected in the pane decides chat or terminal, over what the session was launched as; plain shells and unsupported agents get the terminal.
acceptance: Select a Claude session → chat body; flip Show terminal → raw terminal.
Select a plain shell → terminal body, no switch.
Send a line from the composer → it appears as the agent's next input.

cards.title: Hand one agent's result to another agent
cards.user_does: From a finished session, chooses to send its result to another session.
cards.user_sees: A short list of other chat-capable agents' sessions, the last viewed first; picking one drops the result into that session's composer.
rules: The target list is capped.
Whatever the user already typed in the target composer is kept.
File paths with spaces are quoted.
acceptance: Two other chat sessions exist, one viewed last → it is listed first.
Result path contains a space → it arrives quoted.

cards.title: Add a session from the Agents screen
cards.user_does: Clicks + on an agent group, or sees the empty state on a fresh profile.
cards.user_sees: A new not-yet-started session preset appears under that agent; with no agents an empty state invites building one.
rules: The preset waits for the user to pick and start it.
acceptance: Click + under an agent → a not-started row appears and is selected.

cards.title: Custom-agent builder from the Agents screen
cards.user_does: Clicks + beside the agents heading or the empty-state call to build an agent.
cards.user_sees: The custom-agent builder.
rules: Owner cut with its settings page; the department-agents plan wants a successor.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: custom-agent builder dropped with the your-agents settings section. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Board columns and card status chips
cards.user_does: Opens Board.
cards.user_sees: Every session as a card in a lane by status, each with a chip: Working with age and current step, Needs you naming the approval, Stopped, Done with the first line of the final message and a link to the newest file written, Can't reach, Starting, or Setup needed.
rules: A stale working signal never shows Working.
A plain shell terminal gets no chip.
A stop caused by a limit or sign-in reads Stopped, never Done.
The newest written file wins; the path is absolute.
A working card shows how long it has been working and its current step in plain words.
acceptance: Agent stopped by usage limit → card in a stopped state, chip says Stopped.
Agent finished → chip shows first line of its last message.
Agent writes a.md then b.md and finishes → card points at b.md.

cards.title: Board shows every terminal session in order
cards.user_does: Opens Board with several tabs and splits.
cards.user_sees: One card per terminal pane in tab-group order; panes that were never started appear as chooser cards; cards use the saved agent's name.
rules: Editor and browser tabs never become cards.
A background tab's pane is not borrowed into another card.
acceptance: Two tabs, one split into two panes → three cards in tab order.

cards.title: Approve or deny from a Board card
cards.user_does: Clicks approve or deny on a card that needs permission.
cards.user_sees: The answer goes to that agent and the card moves out of needs-you.
rules: Board keeps its own permission buttons after the terminal-grid footer was removed.
acceptance: Agent asks to run a command → card shows both buttons; approve → agent proceeds.

cards.title: Open a session's live terminal inside its Board card
cards.user_does: Expands a card to see its terminal, then closes it.
cards.user_sees: The live terminal moves into the card; on close it returns to its exact place in the grid.
rules: The process and scrollback are kept; only the view moves.
acceptance: Expand a card, type a command, collapse → the grid pane shows the same output in the same position.

cards.title: Large workspace boards stay smooth
cards.user_does: Opens the sidebar's workspace board, which sorts worktrees into status lanes, with many lanes or cards.
cards.user_sees: Scrolling stays smooth and no lane goes missing.
rules: Only lanes near the viewport are mounted.
A workflow with 21 statuses keeps every lane.
acceptance: Board with hundreds of cards → scrolling stays responsive; marquee over a lane selects all its cards.

cards.title: Swarm pane footer and terminal-grid message bar (retired 2026-10-05)
cards.user_does: Used to answer, approve or deny, or type to an agent from a strip under each terminal pane.
cards.user_sees: No strip under terminal panes any more; typing goes to the terminal, approvals go through Board or the terminal.
rules: Removed in two steps the same day: the message bar first, then the whole footer.
Board keeps its own permission buttons; the Agents screen keeps its composer.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: H: default skip

cards.title: Agent Dashboard drawer
cards.user_does: With the experimental dashboard setting on, opens the drawer (also from a bound shortcut), and launches or types to agents from its cards.
cards.user_sees: Agents bucketed as working, idle, done or blocked; each row shows the agent label with its model, conversation name, buttons to send to it, a question glyph when waiting, red when blocked, tree lines for child agents and an orchestration task preview.
rules: Off by default behind the experimental agent dashboard setting.
A stale working agent decays to idle; acknowledged completions move to idle.
Finished agents stay listed after their tab closes.
Escape closes an open terminal panel inside the drawer before the drawer itself.
Choosing a row reveals its worktree.
Nothing is computed while the drawer is closed, and the drawer stays usable during a burst of 100 status updates.
Its settings menu decides whether idle agents show.
Disabled agents are not offered; user defaults are honoured.
Card context shows the linked GitHub pull request when known.
Ships unbound.
Inert while the experiment is off and while Settings is open.
Its row is hidden in the shortcut list until the experiment is on, which reads as a broken key.
Rows carry the repository icon into the drawer.
A finished agent row never shows a tool as still running.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: H: default skip (improvement card AGENT-7 asks for one control tower on by default; owner to decide)

cards.title: Read-only Runs view in the dashboard
cards.user_does: With the dashboard on, opens its Runs tab.
cards.user_sees: Orchestration runs and their tasks, with refresh and paging; nothing can be dispatched from here.
rules: Creating or routing work stays in the coordinator terminal and CLI.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: H: default skip

cards.title: Dashboard pop-out window and Agent Map (retired 2026-10-05)
cards.user_does: Used to pop the dashboard into its own window or see agents on a map.
cards.user_sees: Neither exists; only the drawer remains.
rules: Retired with the redesign; the drawer was kept.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: H: default skip

cards.title: Desktop pet that reacts to agents
cards.user_does: Turns on the pet experiment.
cards.user_sees: An animated pet over the window that idles, runs while agents work, waits when one is blocked, and celebrates a finished review; it jumps on hover, can be dragged, has a status-bar segment, and custom pet bundles can be imported.
rules: Off by default.
Dragging past a small dead zone makes it run in the drag direction.
It stays clamped inside the window.
It appears only after saved state has loaded.
Sprite sizes are read from the image; a bundle in the Codex pet format gets matching defaults.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: H: default skip

cards.title: Activity page
cards.user_does: Turns on the Activity experiment and opens the page.
cards.user_sees: The Activity feed; if it was open at quit it is restored even when settings fail to load.
rules: Off by default.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: H: default skip

cards.title: Agent Grid page (retired 2026-09-22)
cards.user_does: Used to switch the sidebar to an agent grid.
cards.user_sees: Up to six live terminal tiles per launched worktree, font shrinking from 14 to 12 to 11 as tiles grow.
rules: Went with the sidebar mode switch in the quieter-sidebar pass.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: H: default skip

cards.title: Kolux Mobile page and title-bar button
cards.user_does: Turns on the Kolux Mobile button and opens the page.
cards.user_sees: The phone pairing page.
rules: Button off by default; the page restores even when its button is hidden.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: mobile page and pairing go with area 18 remote and hosts. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Add or remove sessions by shortcut
cards.user_does: Binds and presses the add-session or remove-session command.
cards.user_sees: A session pane is added, or after a confirmation one is removed.
rules: The title-bar −/+ stepper was retired on 2026-10-05; the commands stay.
Both ship unbound.
Remove always asks first.
acceptance: Bind remove, press it → a confirmation appears before any pane closes.

cards.title: Worktree palette: jump anywhere
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+J (Mac) or Mod+Shift+J (Windows, Linux) and types.
cards.user_sees: One list with sections for open tabs, worktrees, projects and project groups, settings pages, quick actions and pull requests or issues; Enter goes there.
rules: The View menu shows the chord as a hint; the renderer owns it.
Archived worktrees are left out.
Pasted queries over the size limit are refused.
acceptance: Type part of a branch name → that worktree is in the list; Enter switches to it.
Type a settings page name → a row that opens that page.

cards.title: Palette ranking
cards.user_does: Types a query in the palette.
cards.user_sees: Exact intent first, then prefix matches, then fuzzy matches; ties go to the most recently active item.
rules: Open tabs lead on a tie; unmatched rows sort after matched ones.
Filler words like go or open are ignored.
A candidate covering only a minority of the query words is dropped.
Accents and CJK text fold so non-Latin words still match.
Every typed word must land on the row; adding a word that matches nothing removes results rather than widening them.
Words containing digits, such as PR or issue numbers, match exactly (with or without #), never fuzzily.
Small typos are forgiven only in long words made of letters.
A single Latin letter matches only the start of a word or a whole word.
Matches on a row's own fields rank ahead of matches found only on its parent project.
Matching stays inside a fixed time budget on very large lists.
acceptance: Two worktrees match equally, one used a minute ago → it is first.

cards.title: Palette list caps and focus return
cards.user_does: Searches something that matches many items, then closes the palette or picks a row.
cards.user_sees: Each section shows up to 20 rows and a more count that adds 20 at a time; on close, focus returns to the previous element, else the terminal, else the editor.
rules: Duplicate keys never leave ghost rows.
acceptance: 50 matches in one section → 20 rows and a 30-more control.
Open from a terminal, Escape → typing goes to that terminal.

cards.title: Palette rows show live agent state and age
cards.user_does: Opens the palette while agents run.
cards.user_sees: A spinner for working, a radio mark for monitoring, a permission mark, an unread dot, a check for freshly done, and an age like 4m, 3h or 2d.
rules: Permission beats unread, unread beats freshly done.
Ages switch from hours to days at two days.
No status work happens while the palette is closed.
Ages read in minutes until a full hour has passed.
acceptance: Agent waiting on approval with unread output → row shows the permission mark.

cards.title: Filter the palette by repository
cards.user_does: Adds filter chips in the palette.
cards.user_sees: Only rows from the chosen repositories remain; chip options show workspace counts.
rules: Several values in one field mean any of them; different fields must all match.
Chips start from the sidebar's current scope.
Repositories sort by workspace count; archived worktrees do not count.
acceptance: Pick two repositories → rows from either remain.

cards.title: Create a worktree and run quick actions from the palette
cards.user_does: Types a name with no match and picks the create row, or types an action word.
cards.user_sees: A new worktree starts from that name; commands that apply right now are listed, each enabled only when its context allows.
rules: Creation actions are lifted out so the palette can close immediately.
Actions that need a worktree or a repo are hidden or disabled without one.
acceptance: Type an unused name → a create row; Enter → worktree created and opened.
No worktree open → worktree-only actions are not runnable.

cards.title: Find pull requests and checks from the palette
cards.user_does: Types a pull request number or title in the palette.
cards.user_sees: Matching pull requests with their check state, from the same data the Checks panel uses.
rules: When the host reports a PR as unlinked, the palette never falls back to an older cached PR result.
acceptance: Type a known PR number → that PR is listed with its check state.

cards.title: Plugin actions in the palette
cards.user_does: Searches for an action a plugin added.
cards.user_sees: Plugin-provided rows in the palette.
rules: Goes with the plugin runtime.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: plugin marketplace and runtime dropped. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Host badges and host-qualified rows in the palette
cards.user_does: Uses the palette with more than one machine connected.
cards.user_sees: A host badge on rows and tabs named per host.
rules: Badges appear only when two or more hosts are connected.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: multi-host workspaces go with area 18 remote and hosts. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Move between worktrees by keyboard
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+Alt+Left or Right, Mod+Shift+Up or Down, or Mod+1 to Mod+9.
cards.user_sees: Back and forward step through visited worktrees, pages and task details; up and down move to the neighbouring worktree; a number jumps to that position in the list.
rules: Deleted worktrees are skipped.
Repeated visits to the same place are stored once.
Order follows the sidebar list.
acceptance: Visit A, B, Tasks; press back twice → on A.
Press Mod+2 → second worktree in the list is active.
cards.compat: keybinding ids worktree.history.back, worktree.history.forward, worktree.navigateUp, worktree.navigateDown, workspace.selectByIndex

cards.title: Jump to the next session that needs you
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+Shift+J (Mac) or Mod+J (Windows, Linux).
cards.user_sees: Focus moves to the next pane waiting on the user.
rules: Its default chord is the palette's chord swapped per platform.
acceptance: Two panes waiting → pressing twice visits both.

cards.title: Delete-workspace and rename-tab shortcuts
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+Shift+Backspace or Mod+R.
cards.user_sees: The delete flow for the hovered or active workspace, or rename on the active chat or terminal tab.
rules: The hovered row wins over the active one.
acceptance: Hover a non-active row, press → delete flow for the hovered workspace.
Terminal tab active, press → its title becomes editable.

cards.title: Switch a tab between chat and terminal
cards.user_does: Toggles a tab's mode.
cards.user_sees: The tab flips between a chat view and the raw terminal; split siblings are untouched.
rules: New drafts for some agents open in chat when their transcript is local.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: H: default skip

cards.title: Left sidebar: show, hide, resize and focus
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+B, drags the sidebar edge, or presses Mod+Shift+0.
cards.user_sees: The sidebar toggles, resizes within limits, or takes keyboard focus on its list.
rules: Saved widths are clamped into range; invalid saved widths fall back to the current width.
A closed sidebar takes no width.
With the sidebar closed the first tab stays visible and the toggle never overlaps the back button.
acceptance: Close with Mod+B → first tab still fully visible.
Drag past the maximum → width stops at the limit.

cards.title: Sidebar card lists projects and their sessions
cards.user_does: Looks at the left sidebar in the new look and clicks a row.
cards.user_sees: A rounded card listing projects with their worktrees and live sessions, each with the right agent's identity; clicking activates it.
rules: Live session counts ignore dead tabs; worktrees with none show no count.
Clicking activates without scrolling the list.
A sleeping worktree switches immediately; it does not wait for terminals to wake.
Every live pane keeps its row with its own agent identity, also after a sleep and reconnect.
In a split tab each pane's row carries that pane's own conversation name; clicking one pane never renames its sibling, and a pane with no live title borrows none.
acceptance: A Cursor pane and a Gemini pane → both listed, neither labelled Claude.
Close a tab → its worktree's count drops.

cards.title: Left sidebar tint
cards.user_does: Chooses a sidebar appearance mode, tint colour and opacity.
cards.user_sees: The left sidebar takes that tint.
rules: Default mode leaves the sidebar untinted.
acceptance: Pick a tint at 50 % → sidebar background changes accordingly.

cards.title: Show or hide sleeping workspaces
cards.user_does: Toggles sleeping workspaces in the sidebar or with a bound shortcut.
cards.user_sees: Sleeping worktrees appear or disappear from the list.
rules: Shown by default.
The default branch is exempt from sleeping by default; an explicit opt-out is kept.
The shortcut ships unbound.
acceptance: Hide them → sleeping rows vanish; restart → still hidden.

cards.title: Per-worktree skip-permissions override
cards.user_does: Sets or clears the skip-permissions mode for one worktree.
cards.user_sees: That worktree's agents follow the override; it survives restarts.
rules: Invalid saved entries are dropped on load.
acceptance: Set it on one worktree, restart → still set; others unaffected.

cards.title: Workspace host scope in the sidebar
cards.user_does: Chooses which machines' workspaces the sidebar shows and in what order.
cards.user_sees: Workspaces filtered and ordered by host.
rules: Defaults to all hosts; invalid saved scopes fall back to all.
Uploads to a remote workspace that has not been placed are held back.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: multi-host scope goes with area 18 remote and hosts. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Right sidebar: open, close, width and remembered tab
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+L, drags its edge, or switches tabs and restarts.
cards.user_sees: The right sidebar toggles, resizes, and comes back on the same tab and width.
rules: Open by default.
An unknown saved tab falls back to Explorer; an old Search tab becomes the Explorer's search view.
Widths above the old 500px cap are kept; a minimum width and a reserved area are enforced.
On Windows its title strip leaves room for the native window buttons and stays draggable.
If its code chunk fails to load, it recovers instead of crashing the window.
acceptance: Close it, restart → still closed.
Set a width of 640px, restart → 640px.

cards.title: Right sidebar tab strip
cards.user_does: Clicks the tab icons at the top of the right sidebar, or presses a panel shortcut.
cards.user_sees: Explorer, Agents (session history), Source Control and Checks; folder workspaces get Attached worktrees and PR Checks instead of the git tabs.
rules: When narrow, extra tabs overflow into a More menu but the active tab stays visible.
If the remembered tab is not available here, the first visible tab is used; a folder workspace's remembered PR Checks wins.
Mod+Shift+E, Mod+Shift+F and Mod+Shift+G open Explorer, Search and Source Control; Checks has an unbound command.
acceptance: Narrow the sidebar → overflow menu appears and the active tab is still shown.
Open a folder workspace → git tabs hidden, Attached worktrees shown.
cards.compat: keybinding ids sidebar.explorer.toggle, sidebar.search.toggle, sidebar.sourceControl.toggle, sidebar.checks.toggle

cards.title: Plugin panels in the right sidebar
cards.user_does: Opens a tab a plugin added to the right sidebar.
cards.user_sees: The plugin's own panel, themed to match, with a watchdog for hung panels.
rules: An uninstalled plugin's tab falls back to another tab; hidden panel errors are announced.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: plugin marketplace and runtime dropped. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Explorer file tree
cards.user_does: Browses the worktree's files in the Explorer tab, or narrows them with the name filter.
cards.user_sees: A tree with the repo name in its toolbar, refresh, expand and collapse, and keyboard movement; a compact name filter keeps only matches and their folders; an empty Explorer offers an add-project row.
rules: The tree updates on its own when files change on disk, including at a drive root.
Refresh shows a spinner and is disabled while running.
Hidden dotfiles can be shown per worktree; only opt-outs are saved.
Keystrokes in text inputs are never taken as explorer shortcuts.
Ignored-path lookups are debounced while typing.
On Windows network shares, paths compare without case and only on whole folder boundaries, so a neighbouring share with a similar name is not treated as inside the tree.
Filtering the tree to a folder does not change which folders stay expanded afterwards.
Hiding and reopening the Explorer on the same worktree keeps its expanded folders; showing another worktree starts fresh.
Pressing Down with nothing focused selects the first row.
acceptance: Create a file in a terminal → it appears in the tree without manual refresh.
Arrow down through the list → selection moves row by row.
Type a file name → only it and its parents show.
No project → the Explorer offers an add-project row.

cards.title: Explorer file operations
cards.user_does: Renames inline, deletes, undoes, copies a path, or drags files.
cards.user_sees: Rename commits when focus leaves and is discarded on Escape; delete removes the selection; undo and redo reverse file operations; paths copy to the clipboard; drags scroll at the edges.
rules: Deleting a folder and a file inside it deletes the folder once.
Delete is the Delete key, or Mod+Backspace on Mac; undo Mod+Z; redo Mod+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y.
Copy path is Mod+Alt+C on Mac and Alt+Shift+C elsewhere; copy relative path is Mod+Alt+Shift+C.
A slow operation never overwrites the result of a newer one.
Clicking the name of the selected row again starts rename; a click on a folder name waits out the double-click time before expanding, so starting a rename never also opens or closes the folder.
On case-sensitive file systems, two selected files whose names differ only by case are both deleted.

Row menus offer only what fits the row: collapse for an expanded folder, find in folder and open in terminal for folders, view for files, and copy as a file to the system clipboard for a single file; a failed system copy shows an error toast.
acceptance: Rename then press Escape → name unchanged on disk.
Select a folder and a file inside it, delete → one delete, no error.
cards.compat: keybinding ids fileExplorer.undo, fileExplorer.redo, fileExplorer.copyPath, fileExplorer.copyRelativePath, fileExplorer.delete

cards.title: Search in files from the right sidebar
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+Shift+F or flips the Explorer to its search view, types a query, clicks a result.
cards.user_sees: Matches grouped by file; clicking opens the file at the match.
rules: Searching from a folder pre-fills the query and limits it to that folder.
A failed search says why instead of showing an empty list; a search with no hits shows no error.
A result opens in the worktree the search ran in, even if the active worktree changed since.
acceptance: Search from a folder's menu → include pattern is that folder.
Break the search tool → an error message, not an empty list.

cards.title: Source Control: changed files list
cards.user_does: Opens Source Control.
cards.user_sees: Changed files in ordered sections, as a list or a tree, with status letters, a path filter, and the file open in the editor highlighted; status updates soon after edits and pushes.
rules: List view is the default.
Submodules can be expanded in place.
Very large change sets show a banner instead of freezing; a huge-repo warning can be dismissed and stays dismissed.
Long lists are virtualised.
The active worktree refreshes first, then visible ones.
Slow refreshes back off.
A push or an upstream ref change triggers a refresh.
An older status result never overwrites a newer one; if a later automatic refresh fails, the last good result stays on screen.
Sections run Changes, Staged, Untracked by default; a setting offers staged-first or untracked-first, and unresolved merge conflicts are always pinned in their own section above the rest.
Tree view folds a chain of single-child folders into one row but never folds a folder that has more than one child.

The highlight follows the kind of tab that is open: an editing tab marks the working-tree row first and the staged row only when there is no working-tree change; a branch-compare tab of the same file highlights none of the pending rows.
acceptance: Change 3 files, open the panel → 3 rows in the right sections.
Type part of a path in the filter → only matching rows.
Edit a file → its status updates within the polling interval.

cards.title: Open a changed file's diff
cards.user_does: Clicks a changed file, or modifier-clicks it, or right-clicks it.
cards.user_sees: A diff preview opens; Mod-, Shift- or Alt-click opens it in a split; the context menu offers stage, unstage, discard and open.
rules: Mod means Cmd on Mac and Ctrl elsewhere; a plain click never splits.
Row action icons that are unavailable still show their tooltip on hover but ignore clicks.
acceptance: Ctrl-click a file on Windows → diff opens in a new split.

cards.title: Commit box with saved drafts and AI message
cards.user_does: Writes a commit message or asks for one to be generated, then commits.
cards.user_sees: A message box per worktree that keeps its draft; a generate button with a spinner; a clear summary and a recovery prompt when a commit fails.
rules: Each worktree has its own draft, kept across switching and panel remounts.
Commit is enabled only when there is something to commit and a message.
Generation uses the user's chosen agent and defaults.
When only submodule pointers changed, Stage All stays the main action in the commit area.
A failed commit is summed up in one line; a details toggle appears only when the full error says more than the summary.
Failures from the lint step of commit hooks are summed up as a lint failure rather than a wall of tool output.
While merge conflicts are unresolved or a git operation is in progress, the message box is disabled and the commit controls are hidden.
Generation settings can be saved as the default for this repository or for every repository; the save control hides once the current choice already is the saved default.
acceptance: Type a draft in worktree A, switch to B and back → draft still there.
Make a hook fail the commit → a summary and a recovery prompt appear.

cards.title: One main git button that changes with the state
cards.user_does: Clicks the main Source Control button or opens its dropdown.
cards.user_sees: The button offers the next sensible step (commit, push, publish, sync or create a pull request); the dropdown lists the alternatives.
rules: After choosing create pull request, the flow carries through commit and push before opening the PR composer.
Labels change width without pushing the sidebar wider.
A branch that differs from its remote only by equivalent patches is steered to Create PR, with Force Push still in the commit area.
Detached HEAD never offers Publish Branch, but still offers Create PR when a compare base is known.
Push choices stay available after the linked PR has merged.
Create PR stays disabled while a newer readiness check is still loading; an older yes never enables it.
When a push or sync picked from the dropdown is running while the main button reads Commit, the spinner shows on the dropdown arrow.
acceptance: Clean tree with unpushed commits → main button pushes.
Pushed branch with no PR → create pull request is offered.

cards.title: Push failures explain themselves
cards.user_does: Pushes and the push fails.
cards.user_sees: A plain error and a recovery prompt; the push target names a fork when pushing to one.
rules: Remote action errors stay visible until dismissed.
The push-target label names the fork remote whether or not its address ends in .git.
Hiding Source Control AI actions also hides the agent fixes offered on a push failure.
acceptance: Push rejected as behind → recovery prompt offers to pull first.

cards.title: Discard changes with confirmation
cards.user_does: Discards a file or all changes in a section.
cards.user_sees: A confirmation; after confirming, the changes are gone.
rules: Discard-all runs per section in a safe order.

The confirmation says what will happen: delete for untracked or newly added files (warning that staged new files are deleted), restore for deleted tracked files, discard for modified ones, in singular or plural form.
acceptance: Discard all in a section → confirmation first; cancel keeps everything.

cards.title: Branch summary against the base branch
cards.user_does: Looks at the top of Source Control.
cards.user_sees: The branch name, how far it is ahead or behind its base, and total lines added and removed.
rules: Line totals are fetched only when needed and refreshed on git status changes.

The line total splits into source, tests and generated rows that add up to the total; without a test count the remainder is labelled non-generated; an empty generated row is left out; figures use grouped digits.
The previous comparison stays on screen while the upstream status is still loading.
Screen readers hear the source, tests and generated split in the summary label even while it is collapsed.
Line counts show the full number, never an abbreviated form like 8.3k.
An off-by-default setting measures the summary against the branch's upstream instead of the base branch; a base pinned for the worktree or the repository still wins while it is on.
The comparison refreshes when git status sees a new head commit, and at least every 30 seconds as a fallback.
acceptance: Commit 10 added lines → the total shows +10.

cards.title: Ask an agent to fix things from Source Control
cards.user_does: Chooses an agent action such as resolving conflicts.
cards.user_sees: A dialog to pick the agent and confirm the prompt; the agent starts in the worktree.
rules: Merge conflicts offer a resolve-conflicts prompt.
When the saved launch choice already matches, the dialog is skipped and the agent starts once on its own.
If the prompt cannot be handed to the started agent, the launch is reported as failed.
acceptance: Create a conflict → resolve-conflicts action available; running it starts an agent.

cards.title: Create or link a pull request from the sidebar
cards.user_does: Starts a pull request from Source Control, or links an existing one.
cards.user_sees: A composer with a generated title and body, a link to the created PR in the header, and a stack map when the PR sits in a stack.
rules: Creation is blocked with a reason when local state is not ready; a manual link to the host is offered as fallback.
AI generation controls hide when source-control AI actions are hidden.
The stack map opens another PR without changing local branches.
When the push goes to a fork, the manual link for opening a pull request on GitHub names the fork owner with the branch so it targets the right repository.
acceptance: Create a PR → header shows its link.
Uncommitted changes → creation blocked with a reason.

cards.title: Git history in the sidebar
cards.user_does: Opens the git history list.
cards.user_sees: Commit subject rows with managed tooltips.
rules: A slow history load never replaces a newer one.
After switching worktrees, the previous worktree history is never shown, even briefly.
acceptance: Make a commit → it appears at the top.

cards.title: Send or clear review notes
cards.user_does: Sends the review notes written on diffs to the agent, or clears them.
cards.user_sees: Notes go to the agent; clearing asks for confirmation.
rules: The send command ships unbound.
acceptance: Clear notes → confirmation before they are removed.

cards.title: Checks panel for the current pull request
cards.user_does: Opens the Checks tab.
cards.user_sees: The pull request's checks with expandable, resizable details, a review header, a merge conflict notice when relevant, and the PR's comments.
rules: The panel follows the worktree of the focused terminal.
When there is no PR it says so plainly rather than showing a stale one.
Checks poll while running and can be refreshed by hand.
A finished check that reports no outcome shows as unresolved, not pending.
A PR the host reports as unlinked is hidden; an older cached PR never takes its place.
A recent "no pull request" answer is reused for a short grace period instead of asking again.
Polling runs only while the panel is visible.
A pull request the user unlinked stays hidden behind a plain notice naming it, with a button to link it again; no create action is offered meanwhile.
acceptance: Focus a terminal in worktree B → panel shows B's PR.
Branch without a PR → panel says there is no review.

cards.title: Create a pull request from the Checks panel
cards.user_does: Starts a review from the Checks panel; modifier-clicks the review link.
cards.user_sees: A create composer when the branch is ready; the review opens in Kolux or the system browser depending on the modifier, with a hint saying which.
rules: The composer opens only when readiness is confirmed; a hard error clears once fixed.
When a push is still needed and readiness is confirmed, the empty state offers one combined push-and-create action.
A readiness answer is tied to the exact worktree, branch and git state and goes stale after about five minutes; a check for one worktree never clears an error shown for another.
acceptance: Branch pushed, no PR → create composer available.

cards.title: PR comments as cards in the sidebar
cards.user_does: Reads pull request comments in the sidebar, reacts, resolves, or queues a thread for the agent.
cards.user_sees: Cards grouped as open, conversation and resolved, or one chronological list; reactions; queued threads acknowledged once the agent starts.
rules: Pressing Enter while composing with an input method does not send.
A batch of queued threads gets one combined reply.
Replies sit indented under the comment they answer; comment text keeps readable sizes, with headings a step above body text and code, tables and small print never shrunk below caption size.
A thread the host cannot reply to is left out of the combined reply instead of failing the batch.
An Add comment button sits in the comments header, after the display options, and opens a composer that posts a new comment on the pull request.
acceptance: Switch to chronological → comments ordered by time.
Queue an open thread → the agent receives it.

cards.title: Folder workspaces: attached worktrees and PR checks
cards.user_does: Opens a folder workspace that spans several repos.
cards.user_sees: An Attached worktrees tab listing its repos' worktrees, and a PR Checks tab rolling up checks across them.
rules: Rows refresh on their own and on demand.
Worktrees created from an attached worktree, at any depth, are listed under it.
A pull request the host reports as unlinked is left out of the rollup.
acceptance: Folder workspace over two repos → both repos' worktrees listed.

cards.title: GitLab merge requests in the Checks panel
cards.user_does: Opens Checks on a GitLab branch.
cards.user_sees: The merge request's pipeline and merge state.
rules: GitLab status is used when no GitHub PR exists.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: GitLab dropped; GitHub is the only kept provider. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Ports in the status bar
cards.user_does: Clicks the ports item in the status bar.
cards.user_sees: Ports the active workspace is listening on, with the URL a dev server printed, an Open button, and a stop button.
rules: Ports are tied to a workspace by their process; URLs are picked up from terminal output and checked against the process.
Open uses the Kolux browser; Shift+Ctrl-click opens the system browser.
Stopping a port that already exited counts as success.
A failed scan names the problem and keeps the last good list.
Open uses the address the dev server printed when known, otherwise plain http on the listening address.
Ports held by processes outside the workspace are listed as external and can never be stopped from here.
A port belongs to the deepest worktree containing its process's working folder, so nested worktrees keep their own ports.
acceptance: Start a dev server on 5173 → port listed with its URL; stop it → it disappears.

cards.title: Ports tab for remote repositories
cards.user_does: Opens the Ports tab on an SSH repository.
cards.user_sees: Forwarded ports of the remote machine.
rules: The tab only appears for SSH repositories; its shortcut is Mac-only.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: SSH hosts go with area 18 remote and hosts. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Agents tab: past sessions for this workspace
cards.user_does: Opens the Agents tab in the right sidebar and chooses workspace, project or all.
cards.user_sees: Past agent sessions in that scope.
rules: Workspace scope is the default.
If the scope is unavailable it falls back automatically and returns later; a manual choice of all stays.
Sessions from a worktree's earlier paths, before a rename, are included.
Project scope also takes in the other worktrees of the same repository.
Once the user picks project or all by hand, the scope never switches back to workspace on its own.
Sessions inside the chosen scope are listed even when they are older than the overall recent-sessions cap.
acceptance: Rename a worktree folder → its older sessions still listed.
Choose all → stays on all after switching worktrees.

cards.title: Search, filter and group past sessions
cards.user_does: Types in the session search, picks agents, or changes grouping.
cards.user_sees: Matching sessions grouped by folder, agent or project, with short labels.
rules: Search takes plain words, quoted phrases, and repo: and path: filters.
Empty sessions can be hidden, but sessions with recoverable content are kept.
Compact labels use the last two path parts.
Paths with accented or non-Latin characters group as one project however their characters are encoded.
An oversized pasted search returns no results at once rather than scanning every session.
A project with a blank setup path never matches every session.
acceptance: Search repo:kolux fix → only that repo's sessions mentioning fix.

cards.title: Session list view options persist
cards.user_does: Changes sort, grouping, agents shown or history depth, or resets them.
cards.user_sees: Choices stay after restart; a counter shows how many options differ from defaults.
rules: Empty sessions are shown by default.
History depth can be set to Unlimited.
acceptance: Change grouping, restart → same grouping; reset → counter clears.

cards.title: Session list refreshes without stealing keystrokes
cards.user_does: Returns to the tab, presses refresh, or starts an agent in Kolux.
cards.user_sees: The list updates; the refresh button forces a full rescan; a new session appears soon after it starts.
rules: Refocus refreshes from cache.
An agent start triggers a throttled rescan.
Results publish only once terminal typing is quiet, at most one second late.
Reopening the tab reuses the last results.
acceptance: Type steadily in a terminal during a refresh → no visible lag.
Start Claude → its session shows in the list without manual refresh.

cards.title: Session rows show prompt, latest turn, sub-agents and worktree
cards.user_does: Reads or expands a session row.
cards.user_sees: The agent, model when recorded, the first prompt, a preview of the latest turn, child runs with state dots, and a worktree line saying current, active or unavailable that jumps there.
rules: When only a preview exists the prompt card says it is a recent prompt.
Choosing a menu action does not expand the row.
Text the agent harness injects into a user turn is not shown as the user prompt.
Previews are trimmed to a fixed length without ever splitting an emoji or other multi-part character.
acceptance: Expand a Claude session with sub-agents → each child listed with a state dot.
Session from a deleted worktree → unavailable badge and an explaining tooltip.

cards.title: Resume a past session in a terminal
cards.user_does: Clicks resume, drags a session into a pane, or copies the resume command.
cards.user_sees: A terminal opens in the session's worktree (or the active one) and the agent resumes; the copied command fits the user's shell.
rules: Sessions with no turns cannot be resumed; copy stays available.
The copied command matches PowerShell, cmd or a POSIX shell.
Codex sessions resume against the right home folder and clear inherited ones.
Resume can open in a new split of a chosen tab group.
Agent default arguments from settings are applied.

A past session can be dragged onto a terminal pane: dropping in the middle resumes it as a new tab in that pane's group, dropping on an edge resumes it in a split on that side; a chat session reopens its chat; a drop beside the panes says to drop on one, and a successful drop confirms the session is queued.
The resume command is quoted for the shell the target tab really runs, even when the default shell setting names WSL but the workspace runs on the Windows host.
acceptance: Resume a Claude session from another worktree → terminal opens there and continues the conversation.
Copy the command with PowerShell as shell → it runs as pasted.

cards.title: Resume a past session as chat
cards.user_does: Chooses to resume a session in chat.
cards.user_sees: The session reopens as a chat.
rules: Claude only in its own workspace; Codex anywhere.
Remote and WSL sessions are refused.
acceptance: Claude session from another workspace → chat resume not offered.

cards.title: Continue a session with another agent
cards.user_does: Chooses to continue a past session with the same or a different agent.
cards.user_sees: A new session that carries the transcript, where it stopped, and the original working folder.
acceptance: Continue a Codex session in Claude → Claude starts with the prior transcript.

cards.title: Find the live pane a past session is running in
cards.user_does: Opens a session that is still running.
cards.user_sees: Kolux focuses the existing pane instead of starting a duplicate.
rules: Matched by the provider's session id, else by an unambiguous first prompt.
Sleeping and retained panes count.
acceptance: Session still open in a pane → that pane is focused.

cards.title: Delete, reveal or open a past session's files
cards.user_does: Deletes a session from its row menu, opens its raw log, reveals the file or copies its path.
cards.user_sees: A deleted session leaves the list and its files go to the system trash; the log opens in a read-only tab; reveal opens the system file manager.
rules: Only local, real paths are deletable; symlinks are refused.
A session folder takes its companion files but keeps file history.
An already-missing file counts as deleted.
Blocked rows say in one plain sentence why, naming the agent.
Every cached list drops the row at once.
Only local sessions offer these.
If the log is already open in an editable tab, that tab comes forward with a note that it is already editable instead of opening a second read-only copy.
acceptance: Delete a Claude folder session → companions trashed, file-history kept.
Open log → read-only tab with the transcript.

cards.title: Scan notices in the session list
cards.user_does: Opens the list when something blocked or limited the scan.
cards.user_sees: A short notice: why the list is empty, how many transcripts were skipped, that the scope was cut short, or that a database could not be read.
rules: Notices are de-duplicated and capped.
A skipped transcript alone never turns an empty list into an error notice.
acceptance: Make one transcript unreadable → a skipped-count notice.

cards.title: Session history reads many agents' transcripts
cards.user_does: Uses several agent CLIs over time.
cards.user_sees: Sessions from all of them in one list, with titles.
rules: Claude: sub-agents pruned, working-folder drift handled, generated titles used.
Codex: both session roots merged without duplicates; worker sessions excluded; its title index used.
Kimi, Grok, Devin, Cline, Antigravity, OMP, Rovo, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw, Copilot and Pi are also read.
An agent's own session-folder override is used exactly as given, ahead of the default agent folder.
Claude Code keeps each project under a folder named after its path with every character that is not a letter or digit replaced by its own dash; the scan finds folders the same way.
acceptance: Run one Claude and one Codex session → both listed with titles.
cards.compat: reads the on-disk session transcripts of the listed agent CLIs

cards.title: Session scans run in the background and survive restarts
cards.user_does: Opens the list on a machine with thousands of sessions.
cards.user_sees: The list fills without freezing the window, and is quick again after a restart.
rules: Scans run in a separate background process that restarts on failure.
Parsed results are cached on disk with a version stamp.
Overlapping scans merge; one window cancelling does not cancel another's.
A stalled WSL disk never hangs the scan.
Only WSL distributions that are already running are searched; a stopped one is never started for a scan.
acceptance: Restart Kolux → the list appears faster than the first cold scan.

cards.title: Tab titles follow session names
cards.user_does: Runs an agent whose session gets a title.
cards.user_sees: The terminal tab takes that title and updates when it changes.
rules: A missing title is retried soon; titles are read in the background.
A sleeping tab keeps its recovered title.
acceptance: Claude names a session → the tab shows that name.

cards.title: Past sessions on remote machines
cards.user_does: Browses or resumes sessions stored on an SSH host, WSL or a paired runtime.
cards.user_sees: Remote sessions merged into the list and resumable on that machine.
rules: Host scope defaults to the workspace's host.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: remote hosts, WSL execution and pairing go with area 18. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Handoff note autosaves
cards.user_does: Writes in a workspace's handoff note.
cards.user_sees: A small state: unsaved, saving, saved, or an error; the text is never lost.
rules: A failed save keeps the buffer and shows an error.
acceptance: Type, wait → saved; make the save fail → error shown, text intact.

cards.title: Status bar: show, hide and choose items
cards.user_does: Toggles View > Appearance > Show Status Bar, or right-clicks the bar.
cards.user_sees: The bar appears or disappears; the right-click menu lists items to show or hide.
rules: Clicking inside an item's popover never opens the visibility menu.
Old saved item lists migrate.
Items for agent CLIs not on the PATH are hidden.
Status bar copy is translated.
acceptance: Right-click the bar, untick Resource Manager → it disappears and stays gone after restart.

cards.title: Keep the computer awake while agents run
cards.user_does: Uses the keep-awake item in the status bar.
cards.user_sees: The current keep-awake mode and whether agents are active.
rules: Off by default.
Not shown on a paired web client.
acceptance: Turn it on and start an agent → item shows awake with agent activity.

cards.title: Resource Manager: memory and CPU per worktree
cards.user_does: Clicks the resource item in the status bar, then a session row.
cards.user_sees: The terminal session count and a popover breaking memory and CPU down by repo and worktree, including browser tabs; picking a row closes the popover and focuses that pane.
rules: Memory figures carry plain caveats about what they measure.
A warning appears when memory commit passes 60 % and again at 80 %.
Browser rows are read-only.
Nothing polls while the popover is closed.
A Space scan result hands off as ready.
Terminals left over from a layout whose tab is gone are not counted.
Sessions started in the background are counted without their pane being on screen.
Sessions that cannot be tied to a worktree are listed in their own unattributed group instead of being dropped.
acceptance: Open with three agents → each worktree shows memory and CPU.
Press Enter on a row → its pane has focus.

cards.title: Kill a terminal session from the Resource Manager
cards.user_does: Clicks kill on a session row, or uses Manage Sessions.
cards.user_sees: A confirmation, then the session ends and the count drops; Manage Sessions also ends sessions the daemon holds that no window owns.
rules: Confirmation is skipped only when the session is proven already gone.
Agent-owned sessions are never offered for cleanup.
Until the window has finished loading its workspaces, no session is shown as attached to a pane.
acceptance: Kill a foreign daemon session → session count drops by one.

cards.title: Skill and app update progress in the status bar

Tasks button and app name are on by default; Automations button is off.

cards.title: Saving the workspace when Kolux quits
cards.user_does: Quits Kolux with work open.
cards.user_sees: On relaunch every workspace and tab returns; unsaved editor changes block a silent quit.
rules: A failed save is retried, then falls back to a durable-only save.
Restored workspaces rebuild their tab layouts in session order in one pass.
acceptance: Quit with three tabs → relaunch shows the three tabs.
Quit with an unsaved editor buffer → prompt, no silent loss.

cards.title: Terminals keep their scroll position across view switches
cards.user_does: Switches worktree or screen while an agent streams output, then comes back.
cards.user_sees: The terminal is where it was: pinned to the bottom if it was, or at the same scrolled spot.
rules: Hidden terminals are parked to save memory and come back intact.
Full-screen programs still get mouse-wheel events after a switch.
acceptance: Scroll up during a stream, switch away and back → same scroll spot.

cards.title: Keyboard layouts, Option as Alt and key protocols
cards.user_does: Types in terminals on a non-US layout, on a Mac with Option, in a full-screen program, or through an input method.
cards.user_sees: Shortcuts match the printed keys; Option acts as Alt or types symbols as the layout suggests; extended keys like Shift+Enter reach programs; Enter that confirms an input-method composition never sends.
rules: Kolux detects the layout and follows layout changes on Mac.
Left and right Option are tracked separately.
Off on the native Windows console unless the agent needs it.
The protocol resets cleanly after the program exits.
While an input method is composing, every key goes to it, shortcut chords such as the palette chord included; the same chord outside composition works as usual.
acceptance: German layout → shortcut labels use the layout's characters.
Run an agent that needs extended keys on Windows → Shift+Enter works.
Compose with an IME, press Enter → text confirmed, no submit.

cards.user_sees: Copies work up to set limits and show feedback; programs can copy to the clipboard by default.

acceptance: Copy over the limit → clear message, no crash.

cards.title: First-run notification permission
cards.user_does: Starts Kolux for the first time on a Mac.
cards.user_sees: One welcome notification that asks for permission; never asked again once answered.
rules: Other platforms are reported unsupported and never probed.

acceptance: Fresh Mac profile → one prompt; restart → none.

cards.title: Import setup scripts from other tools' configs

cards.user_sees: Setup and teardown commands offered for import.

Oversized or malformed files are refused before parsing.

cards.title: Markdown view preferences

cards.title: The shell avoids needless redraws
cards.user_does: Works with many tabs and agents.
cards.user_sees: The window stays responsive.
rules: Unrelated settings or store changes do not redraw the shell's surfaces.
acceptance: Change an unrelated setting → no visible flicker of the workspace.

cards.title: Confirmation prompts: Enter, Escape and don't ask again
cards.user_does: Is asked to confirm an important or destructive action, such as deleting or discarding.
cards.user_sees: A small dialog with Cancel focused; Escape backs out; some prompts offer a don't-ask-again box.
rules: Cancel holds focus when the dialog opens, so a stray Enter does not confirm.
Enter confirms only on prompts that opt in, and only while the confirm button has focus.
Escape always cancels.
The don't-ask-again choice is saved only when the user confirms; backing out saves nothing, and the tick does not carry into the next prompt.
acceptance: Open a delete prompt and press Enter: nothing is deleted.
Tick don't ask again, press Escape: the next prompt still appears, unticked.
Tick don't ask again and confirm: that prompt no longer appears.

cards.title: Hover-only buttons stay visible on touch screens
cards.user_does: Uses Kolux on a touch screen or pen, where nothing can hover.
cards.user_sees: Row action buttons that a mouse user sees only on hover are shown all the time.
rules: Applies to every hover-revealed action: sidebar rows, the past-session list, checks, ports and status-bar popovers.
With a mouse the buttons still stay hidden until hover.
acceptance: Touch-only device: row actions are visible without hovering. Mouse: hidden until hover.

cards.title: Select changed files and stage or unstage them together
cards.user_does: Right-clicks a changed file in Source Control, or extends a selection of changed files, then uses the bar that appears under the list.
cards.user_sees: A bar along the bottom of the changed-files list with how many files are selected, a Stage button and an Unstage button that each carry how many of the selected files they apply to, and a clear button; the list leaves room so its last row stays visible.
rules: Right-clicking a row that is not selected makes it the selection, so the context menu and the bar act on it.
Stage and Unstage show only when at least one selected file can take that action; while the action runs the buttons are disabled and a spinner replaces the count.
Escape, the clear button, a click outside the list, or switching between list and tree view clears the selection.

A selected file that leaves the visible list (filtered out, staged elsewhere, refreshed away) drops out of the selection; a range anchor that is no longer visible is forgotten and the next range click behaves like a plain click.
A range runs in visible order across sections; Mod-click toggles a single row.
At 0.15.0 Mod-, Shift- and Alt-click open the file in a split before selection is considered, so building a multi-row selection with the mouse is shadowed; the owner decides which gesture wins.
acceptance: Right-click an unstaged changed file → the bar shows 1 selected and a Stage (1) button; press Escape → the bar disappears.
Select a file, then filter the list so the file is hidden → the selection empties and the bar hides.
With a selection showing, click outside the Source Control list → the selection clears.
Click Stage in the bar → the button disables with a spinner until staging finishes, then the files move to the staged section.
